summary.text: 清 means “clear,” “pure,” or “clean.” 氵 supplies the idea of water and 青 supplies the sound. The character’s early meaning was the appearance of clear water, so its structure connects a visible quality with a pronunciation cue.

formation.text: 水 supplies meaning and 青 supplies pronunciation.

components.text: 氵 is the compressed side form of 水, “water.” It is a positional variant, with the same semantic function.
The entire 青 component provides sound. It functions here as one phonetic unit; its own internal parts do not separately explain 清.

sound.text: Component and character have the same modern syllable and tone.
The reconstructed forms differ in vowel length, shown by ː. Their remaining sounds match.

history.text: Bronze and manuscript forms already show the pairing of water and 青. Later uses extend beyond visibly clear water: early manuscript examples include pure wine and the use of 清 for the word “quiet,” otherwise written 靜.

An Old Chinese reconstruction pairs 清 *sʰleŋ with 青 *sʰleːŋ. The closely matching sounds explain the phonetic choice. The asterisks indicate reconstructed forms; the length mark in the second form distinguishes the proposed vowel lengths.
